chapter: Biddle, Durham and early road shows
title: Escape artist, comedians and the medicine show's break-up in Cincinnati
summary: He describes the show's acts, including an escape artist who expanded his chest against the ropes, and how the show broke up after Greensboro and Cincinnati.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: And now, here's -- we had -- what we would do -- we had a nice little show. We had comedians and an escape artist. We had a fellow -- we had some big men would come up and tie that fellow -- tie him and he would get loose, just like that. They would come up there to tie and when they tied him we would be playing -- while they tied him we was playing da-de-da-de -- and they would just tie him up, but when the people get through tying him up, then we would hit into something fast, you know, we'd hit into something fast and after a while he'd start shaking and chord, he'd step right out of them. The cord.
told us how he did that. He'd expand -- he would expand his chest when they were tying him --
Yes, and while they was tying him he'd expand everything this way. They'd be tying and the way he stood -- then, when he relaxed and straightened up, well -- there's tricks to all trades.
So, we played awhile and then in Greensboro, North Carolina. Then we left Greensboro, North Carolina and went to Cincinnati, Ohio.
The medicine show did. And then I sent my wife back home to stay until we could get a place. Well, we stayed there for awhile and the medicine show broke up there.
Where was home? Arkansas or Durham?
